The image shows soybean seeds held in a hand. The seeds display a clear mix of:
- Normal yellow/tan seed coats on some seeds
- Prominent **pink to purple discoloration** on the seed coats of many seeds, ranging from partial blotches to nearly fully purple-covered seeds

This is a textbook presentation of **Purple Seed Stain**, caused by *Cercospora kikuchii*. The symptom description states: "Pink to purple discoloration on seed coats of infected seeds; soybean pods infected by C. kikuchii develop purple seed stain." The image matches perfectly — soybean seeds with variable degrees of purple/violet discoloration on the seed coat, exactly as described.

No other class in the list involves seed coat discoloration of this type. Bean Pod Mottle virus can cause seed mottling but not this specific pink-to-purple pattern.
